Owner's fix round for the Notre-Dame kit (v1 -> v2): one more tower fix. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the
chevet, the flying buttresses, the flanks, the lit glass and floodlights, the spire, the roofs, the west front's portals
and rose, the plot and its size. Read /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/paris/notre-dame/04-west-facade-day.jpg and /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/paris/notre-dame/concept-notre-dame.jpg first.
Fix only the two west towers. Each face of each tower now shows rows of thin slits, which read as a modern block:
1. BELFRY OPENINGS. Replace the slits with the real belfry stage: on all four faces of both towers, in the upper third,
   two very tall, narrow POINTED lancet openings side by side (each about 3 wide and 14-18 tall, a stepped pointed head),
   set back in a deep reveal (two blocks), dark inside (dark oak trapdoors as louvres or black stained glass), with a
   slender colonnette (a wall) between them and a pointed hood moulding over the pair.
2. Below the belfry stage, a band of blind tracery / a smaller arcade, then plain ashlar; a projecting string course
   (stairs or slabs) at the base of the belfry stage and another under the top.
3. TOPS. An openwork parapet (walls or iron bars under a stone rail) with a small pinnacle at each corner, around the flat
   dark lead roof.
4. Clasping buttresses at the tower corners, proud by one block, stepping back as they rise.
Keep the towers' footprint and overall height; sandstone family as now. Diff only inside the two tower boxes.
summary:
Rebuilt the upper stage of both west towers (y 58..97) from v1.nbt via tower-v2.mjs; everything else is cell-for-cell identical to v1. build.nbt is saved and passes check (no floating blocks).
Slits replaced by a real belfry: two 3-wide pointed lancets per face, 2-deep reveal, colonnette, hood moulding, on all 4 faces of both towers.
Blind arcade band, two string courses, stepped clasping buttresses and an openwork parapet added.
applied: 1. Belfry openings: restored the old 3x25 louvred slits to ashlar, then on all four faces of both towers cut two pointed lancets side by side (each 3 wide, y 71..86, stepped head of upside-down stairs with a cut_sandstone keystone row). Each is a two-block reveal with cut_sandstone jambs and a slab sill, black stained glass panes behind, a sandstone_wall colonnette between them, and a stepped pointed hood moulding over the pair (stair rakes with a chiseled_sandstone apex, y 87..91). I used black glass only and dropped the trapdoor louvres, since the louvres were what read as slits.

2. Below the belfry (y 64..67): a blind arcade of 2-wide niches under stair heads, separated by cut_sandstone piers, with plain ashlar under it (y 59..63). A projecting string course of upside-down stairs sits at the base of the belfry stage (y 70) and another under the top (y 93), all round both towers.

3. Tops: kept the flat lead deck and the 2x2 corner pinnacles (still y 97, so height is unchanged). Made the parapet openwork by replacing most of the y 96 wall cells with iron_bars between posts under the existing cut_sandstone rail.

4. Clasping buttresses: added 1-proud L-shaped buttresses at the tower corners, stepping from 4 to 3 to 2 cells long at y 72 and y 84, with stair caps on each step. The existing 2-proud west buttresses now step back to 1 proud at y 72 with a stair lip. The towers' footprint and the y 97 top are unchanged.

Checked: no floating blocks or new orphans; palette shows only light-on-light notes. Diff against v1 changes 0 cells outside the tower boxes (plus their 1-block-proud buttress cells). I looked at the north, west, south and east tower faces and the tops in close-ups, plus the overall elevations.
skipped: Dark oak trapdoor louvres: not used; black stained glass panes alone give the dark interior, which the brief allowed.
The two new buttress tiers are drawn as plain stepped masonry with stair caps, without extra pinnacle shafts on each step, to keep the corner pinnacles at the original top height (y 97).
The fix is a post-process of v1.nbt (tower-v2.mjs, run by make-v2.sh), not a change to the original generator parts. Running make.sh would regenerate the v1 towers.
